title: fix(service-datasource): Setup → Datasources: Test answers truthfully for the primary datasource and for drivers that cannot introspect; Sync on the primary datasource refuses with the true reason
body:
Fixes #24772
Clause-②: yes (widening)

## What was wrong

Setup → Datasources listed the primary datasource as `default · sqlite · connected`, and that is true. `DefaultDatasourcePlugin` connects it through `DatasourceConnectionService` with `asDefault`, and ADR-0062 registers its driver under the driver's own name (`com.objectstack.driver.sql`), not under `default`. Test and Sync then introspected by the name `default`. The engine's registry has no entry by that name, so both answered `[ObjectQL] Datasource 'default' has no registered driver to introspect.`: Test as `200 { ok: false }`, Sync as `400 EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR`. A connected `memory` datasource got the same `ok: false` from Test, because Test was an introspection round trip and that driver has no `introspectSchema`.

Measured before the change, on `origin/main` `c3a8e07b6`, through the real admin routes over a real `ObjectQL` engine, the real connection service and the real `ExternalDatasourceServicePlugin`:

```text
POST /api/v1/datasources/default/test          -> 200 {"ok":false,"error":"[ObjectQL] Datasource 'default' has no registered driver to introspect."}
GET  /api/v1/datasources/default/remote-tables -> 400 EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR, same message
POST /api/v1/datasources/qa_ram/test (memory)  -> 200 {"ok":false,"error":"[ObjectQL] Driver for datasource 'qa_ram' does not support introspectSchema()."}
admin list                                     -> default status "ok", qa_ram status "ok"
```

## What changed (route D, as the seat ruled, comment 6287770114)

All of it is in `packages/services/service-datasource/src`. Nothing in `packages/objectql`.

- **One resolver, reused.** `registeredDriverName()` in `datasource-connection-service.ts` is the default-driver resolver `DatasourceConnectionService.disconnect()` applied inline. It is extracted, and `disconnect()` calls it with its own `asDefault` flag, so its behaviour is unchanged. The Test path calls the same function. `disconnectAll()` names the reserved datasource through the same constant.
- **Test, `POST /api/v1/datasources/:name/test`.** The plugin wires a new optional `liveDriver` seam: the engine's registry entry under the name `registeredDriverName()` resolves. `testConnection()` then:
  - for the primary datasource, answers the driver's `checkHealth()`, giving `{ ok: true, latencyMs }`, and does not introspect the platform database;
  - for a driver with no `introspectSchema` (`memory`, `mongodb`), answers `checkHealth()` with the answer's existing keys, `{ ok: true, latencyMs }` and no `tableCount`, instead of `ok: false`;
  - for a registered driver whose health check fails, answers `ok: false` with a reason;
  - for every other datasource, and for one with no live driver, runs the same introspection round trip as before, with the same `tableCount` and the same engine message.
- **Sync on the primary datasource.** `listRemoteTables`, `generateObjectDraft`, `importObject` and `refreshCatalog` refuse `default` before any introspection. The status and code are the ones each door served before: `400 EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR`, or `EXTERNAL_IMPORT_ERROR` on the import. The message is now the true reason: `Datasource 'default' is the platform's managed primary datasource, not a federation source: its tables are the platform's own objects, so there are no remote tables to list, draft or import from it. Sync objects from an external datasource instead.`

## The measured choice for Test on `default`: `checkHealth()`, not introspection by the resolved name

Both reach the live driver. `checkHealth()` was chosen for three reasons:

- Introspection costs a round trip per table of the platform database. Measured with the real `SqlDriver` on SQLite in memory: `introspectSchema()` took 14.0 ms at 10 tables and 132.0 ms at 120 tables. `checkHealth()` took 0.79 ms and 0.28 ms. On a networked Postgres, each of those per-table round trips also pays the network latency.
- The connection question is what Test asks, and `checkHealth()` is that question (`SELECT 1` on SQL, `ping` on MongoDB).
- The primary datasource is not a federation source, so a `tableCount` of the platform's tables answers nothing the page uses. No consumer in either repository reads `tableCount`.

Every other datasource keeps the introspection probe and its `tableCount`, so nothing moves for a federation source.

## The seat's premises, re-checked before editing

- **P1, holds.** The resolver `disconnect()` applied (`opts.asDefault ? engine.getDefaultDriverName() : name`) needs only `getDefaultDriverName` and `getDriverByName`. Both are on the `'data'` engine's published contract (`IDataEngine`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts`), which the plugin already reads. No objectql change is needed.
- **P2, holds.** The Setup driver catalog (`driver-catalog.ts`) lists `memory`, `sqlite`, `postgres`, `mysql` and `mongodb`. The two without `introspectSchema` have `checkHealth()`: `MemoryDriver.checkHealth()` returns `true`, and `MongoDBDriver.checkHealth()` runs `db.command({ ping: 1 })`. `IDataDriver` declares `checkHealth()` as required.

## Evidence after the change

`packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/primary-datasource-test-and-sync.test.ts` has 10 cases. They run through the real composition: a real `ObjectQL` engine (its source, through this package's vitest alias), the connection service connecting `default` with `asDefault` exactly as `DefaultDatasourcePlugin.init()` does, the plugin's real wiring, and the admin routes over Hono.

- On `default`, the list reads `ok`, and Test answers `200 { ok: true, latencyMs }` with no `error` and no `tableCount`. The driver's `introspectSchema` is never called.
- On `default`, `remote-tables` and `object-draft` answer `400`, with `error.code` `EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR` and the true message. The import refuses with `{ code: 'EXTERNAL_IMPORT_ERROR', status: 400 }`, and the list and catalog refresh with `{ code: 'EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR', status: 400 }`. The platform database is never introspected.
- A `memory` datasource tests `{ ok: true, latencyMs }`, exactly those two keys. A registered driver whose health check answers `false` or throws gives `ok: false`.
- Preservation: a managed runtime SQLite datasource still tests `{ ok: true, tableCount: 1 }` and still lists its tables with `200`. That is the seat's ban on changing Sync for other managed datasources. Sync on `memory` still refuses with the engine's reason. A datasource with no live driver still answers `ok: false`.

Ablations, one behaviour each. Each was run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit once, the on-disk blob changed, and the restore was proven blob == HEAD with an empty `git diff HEAD`. The subject is this package's own source, imported relatively, so no build sits between the mutation and the reading.

| leg | mutation | reading |
|:---|:---|:---|
| A1 | the Test path looks the driver up by the datasource name, not through `registeredDriverName` | red, 1 failed: `expected { ok: false, …(1) } to match object { ok: true }` |
| A2 | route A put back: no primary guard on `listRemoteTables`, and introspection resolves the default | red, 2 failed: `expected 200 to be 400`, and `listRemoteTables('default')` resolved a value |
| A3 | a driver without `introspectSchema` goes back to the introspection round trip | red, 2 failed: `expected { ok: false, …(1) } to match object { ok: true }` (re-run at `3226d4019`) |
| A4 | Test on `default` introspects by the resolved name | red, 1 failed: `expected [ 'latencyMs', 'ok', 'tableCount' ] to deeply equal [ 'latencyMs', 'ok' ]` (re-run at `3226d4019`) |
| A5 | a failed health check is ignored | red, 1 failed: `expected true to be false` |
| A6 | the dropped `introspection` key put back on a driver that cannot introspect | red, 1 failed: `expected [ 'introspection', 'latencyMs', 'ok' ] to deeply equal [ 'latencyMs', 'ok' ]` (at `3226d4019`) |

## The published-surface addition: Clause-② yes (widening)

`ExternalDatasourceServiceConfig` is exported from the package's `.` entry, so its new optional member `liveDriver` widens the published surface. The changeset is a `minor` bump that declares `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and names that member. No status code, error code or accepted value moves on any route. Test's answer keeps its existing keys (`ok`, `latencyMs`, `tableCount`, `error`): the `introspection` key from the first head was dropped, because nothing reads it.

- `ExternalDatasourceServiceConfig.liveDriver?`: a host that builds the service without it keeps the old probe.

`registeredDriverName` and `DEFAULT_DATASOURCE_NAME` are module exports only, not exported from the package entry.

## Acceptance notes

- **`refreshCatalog` is included under the bounded in-place exemption.** It is the same defect class (the same false "no registered driver" answer for `default`), in the same file, through the same refusal helper. Its door (`POST …/external/refresh-catalog`) keeps `400 EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR`.
- **A boundary, checked by reading the code.** The refusal is keyed on the host-reserved name `default` (ADR-0062). The only way to register a driver literally named `default` is `ObjectQL.create({ datasources: { default: driverWithNoName } })`. A repository grep finds no production caller of `ObjectQL.create`, and every in-tree driver carries its own name. So no in-tree composition answered `200` on Sync for `default` before this change.
- **The card's "no edit or delete" is by design, not a defect.** The tester's own `38-integrations-datasources-created.png` shows Edit and Delete on the runtime `qa_mem` row. Only the code-origin `default` row lacks them: code-defined datasources are read-only (`datasource-admin-service.ts` header), and objectui hides both on `origin: 'code'`.
- **Not in this PR, per the ruling.** `ObjectQL.introspectDatasource` still does not apply ADR-0062 (no objectql edit). Sync on other managed runtime datasources is unchanged (route B, filed separately by the seat). The two objectui renderer findings are filed by the seat.
- **Noted, not filed: the draft probe discards the answer of `checkHealth()`.** `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin.probe`, behind `POST /api/v1/datasources/test`, awaits `driver.checkHealth()` and ignores the boolean it returns, so a draft whose driver's health check answers `false` would report `ok: true`. This comes from reading the code only: no public-door reading was taken.

## Verification

At HEAD `3226d4019` (no further merge of `origin/main`: no conflict and no main-caused red, AGENTS.md §10):

- `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/service-datasource^...' build`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-datasource build`: exit 0, and `check-dts-emitted` reports 4/4.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-datasource typecheck`: exit 0. `--listFiles` includes the new test file.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-datasource test`: 48 files, 862 tests passed, 47.6 s.
- Gate families from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (69 commands): 68 exited 0 and 1 was not measured. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: it reads every package's built output, and this worktree builds only this package's closure), so CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` is its reading. `--ran` reconciliation: `69 derived, 68 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, with an exit code on every line. `node scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs` is not owed: no exported symbol is renamed or deleted.

`test:repo` was not run locally. CI owns it, and this diff touches no test of that project.
